Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply surgical code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD — modify ONLY the files and lines required to resolve open review threads, merge conflicts, or owned CI failures, and NEVER rewrite or refactor untouched/already-approved code in the PR, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input//` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input//`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, ci_classification.json, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see the TDD approach section included later in this prompt — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P5_CLASS["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_classification.json — machine-classified check failures (infra vs owned)"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P8["8️⃣ input/TICKET/review_policy.md — the resolved reviewPolicy: which severities trigger this lap, density cap, downgrade protocol"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P5_CLASS --> P6 --> P7 --> P8 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. When `input//ci_classification.json` is present (`[{ "name", "class": "infra|owned", "confirmedBy": "base|other-pr|none" }]`), read it first: - Leave checks classified as `"class": "infra"` alone (do not spend rework commits trying to fix runner/network failures already confirmed on the base branch) and note them under foreign/infra reds in `outputs/response.md`. - Fix every check classified as `"class": "owned"` (including `confirmedBy: "other-pr"` or `"none"`). Never classify a check as `infra` yourself — `ci_classification.json` is the sole authority. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## 4. Downgrade protocol — ⚠️→💡 only with a written justification `review_policy.md` carries the resolved severity table: the tiers whose round is `rework` gate approval and trigger this lap; polish/none tiers do not. Fix in that order (🚨 first, then ⚠️). You may downgrade a **specific** ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only when you write the justification into the census** — both the thread reply and the response summary must state why the finding is NOT real maintainability debt (e.g. the guarded condition is unreachable, the contract is documented elsewhere, the risk is structurally impossible). The next review round honors a justified downgrade: the finding counts 💡 and the cycle converges to APPROVE **without a code change**. - A silent downgrade does not exist — without the written justification the finding stays ⚠️ and the review re-raises it, repeating the loop. - Downgrade the finding, not the conversation: still reply to the thread (the reply IS the justification carrier). - Never downgrade 🚨 BLOCKING — only the reviewer (or the project `reviewPolicy` config) can weaken a blocking finding. ## 5. Opportunistic pickup — cheap 💡/🪶 ride the lap While the lap fixes its mandatory set (🚨/⚠️), pick up the cheap findings you pass anyway: - **Eligible:** 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT findings in the SAME files your mandatory fixes already touch — you are in the file, the change is doc/test-trivial, and the lap budget allows it: `review_policy.md` carries `opportunisticMaxThreads` (default 8) and `opportunisticSameFilesOnly` (default true). Stay inside both. - **Not eligible (leave for triage):** findings in files the mandatory set does not touch, findings needing >trivial edits, and anything non-local to this PR's diff. Skipping them is correct — the machine triage closes non-picked threads with `wontfix`/`deferred` dispositions after the lap lands; do NOT force-fix them here. - **Bookkeeping:** every picked-up thread still gets its `outputs/review_replies.json` entry; name the fixing commit in the reply so the machine can close it as `fixed: `. Threads you did not pick up need no reply — triage owns them. ## 6. Surgical Scope Guard — never rewrite approved code outside the findings In `pr_rework`, you are modifying an existing PR that has already been implemented and reviewed: - **Modify ONLY** the files and code regions directly required to resolve: 1. Open review threads (`pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json`), 2. Merge conflicts (`merge_conflicts.md`), or 3. Owned CI failures (`ci_failures.md` / `ci_violations.json` / `ci_classification.json`). - **DO NOT** refactor, reformat, rename, reorganize imports, or rewrite untouched/already-approved parts of the PR diff (even if your session started fresh without prior history). - Keep the rework commit diff minimal and strictly scoped to the open findings so reviewers can verify each fix in isolation. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## tdd_test_directory.md # TDD Test Directory Rules Write failing unit tests in the repository's existing unit-test tree **only**: - Discover the unit-test directory from the existing build and test configuration and from nearby tests for the code being changed. - Follow the naming, layout, and test-runner conventions already established in that directory. ❌ **Never** place development TDD tests under `testing/`. `testing/` is owned by test-automation agents (regression probes, workflow observation tests, accessibility gates, etc.). If your production changes break existing tests there, leave them untouched and mention the breakage in `outputs/response.md` so the test-automation agent can update them. ## git_completion_guard.md # Git Completion & Closing-Keyword Guard - **Completion guard**: Before writing `outputs/response.md`, run `git fetch origin && git log "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD | cut -d/ -f2)..HEAD" --oneline`. An empty result means your commits did not land — re-do or resume the work before declaring completion. - **No closing keywords in commits or PR bodies**: Do NOT include `Fixes #...`, `Closes #...`, or `Resolves #...` against tracker tickets unless explicitly instructed; ticket lifecycle transitions are managed by the post-action workflow. ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## output_rules.md ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. All output must be Markdown. ### Required files 1. `outputs/response.md` - Markdown fix summary for the top-level PR comment. - Use `#`/`##` headings, ` ``` ` code fences, `-` bullets. - Required sections: `## Issues/Notes`, `## Approach`, `## Files Modified`, `## Test Coverage`. - **Owned CI violations & check classification**: when `ci_classification.json` is present, leave `"class": "infra"` checks alone (mention them in a foreign/infra section) and never reclassify an `"owned"` check as `infra` yourself. When `ci_failures.md` has a "Violations you must fix (N owned)" table, list EVERY owned violation with `fixed` (what changed) or `disputed: ` (why the gate is wrong). A summary claiming the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected — the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts it. 2. `outputs/review_replies.json` - **Mandatory** when the PR has open review threads. - If there are no open threads, write `{ "replies": [] }`. - Format: ```json { "replies": [ { "inReplyToId": 1234567890, "threadId": "", "reply": "outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md" } ] } ``` 3. `outputs/review_replies/*.md` - One Markdown file per open PR review thread. - The file path is referenced from `outputs/review_replies.json` via the `reply` field. - Keep each reply concise and factual; reference the fix location when possible. Rules for review replies: - Read `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` to obtain each open thread's `threadId` and `rootCommentId` (`inReplyToId`). - Create one reply entry and one `.md` file for **every** open review thread — do not skip any unresolved conversation. - `threadId` is required to resolve/close the conversation; `inReplyToId` is required to post the reply in the correct thread. - ⚠️ **Copy `threadId` verbatim, character-for-character, from `pr_discussions_raw.json`.** Its format depends on which SCM the PR lives on (a GitHub GraphQL node ID, a GitLab discussion hash, an ADO thread number, etc.) and is opaque — never invent, prefix, reformat, or pattern-match it against an example. The value above is a placeholder showing *where* the field goes, not what it should look like. - Do **not** put the reply body inline in the JSON; use the `reply` field only as a file path reference. - ⚠️ **Common mistake**: `pr_discussions_raw.json` uses the field names `rootCommentId` and `body`. When writing `review_replies.json`, you MUST rename these to `inReplyToId` and `reply` respectively — do NOT copy the input field names as-is into the output JSON, or the reply will silently post as an untargeted top-level comment instead of a threaded reply. ### Blocked Rework only reworks: it fixes the open review threads in code and never asks questions (questions belong to the refinement agents). Every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. If you hit a problem you genuinely cannot get past, change no thread state and write the reason in `outputs/response.md` (start the file with `BLOCKED:` followed by what blocks you and what is needed). A pass with open threads and no code change is treated as blocked: threads are not resolved and the ticket moves to the Blocked status. Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write `outputs/response.md` — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise. ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ## bash_tools.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SHELLSTATE["⚠️ Persistent-shell pitfalls (sandbox-observed)"] P1["Never end commands with exit — it kills the shell session, making read_bash fail with Invalid shell ID"] P2["Capture the exit code via $? right after the command, before running anything else — a late $? reads the wrong command's code"] P3["Avoid $PIPESTATUS — it produced wrong exit codes in the sandbox; redirect output to a file and check $? instead"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end subgraph BGJOBS["⚠️ Long-running commands — background execution, never foreground-poll"] B1["Any command that can run longer than ~2 minutes (full test suite, coverage run, build, dependency install, dev server or watch mode) MUST be started with bash background: true — you get a job id immediately and the completion notice arrives as a message"] B2["❌ NEVER wait for a long job with foreground sleep-polling: repeated sleep-then-check loops like sleep 540 → ls coverage. A foreground sleep pins the tool-call open — owner steering and cancel cannot reach you until it ends — and burns wall-clock plus a runner slot"] B3["While a background job runs, keep working on other steps — check progress between steps with bash_job status / bash_job output <job-id> — never park the turn in a watch loop"] B4["A harness hint like background candidate: bash background: true, job board /tasks, --wait-for-jobs is an ORDER, not a suggestion — obey it and start the command in the background; working around it with foreground sleeps is a violation"] B5["Verification order: finalize ALL code edits BEFORE launching a long verification run (full suite, coverage) — verification must run against a frozen tree, otherwise the run is wasted"] B6["Files changed while a verification run is in flight? Do NOT kill it mid-flight — let it finish, treat the result as stale, then deliberately start a fresh run against the updated tree"] B7["B6 covers a job still making progress — do NOT kill it mid-flight; a job with NO progress for ~10 min (or 2× its expected duration) is HUNG — dispose of it and MOVE ON: bash_job stop <job-id>, note the disposal in the deliverable (job id, command, last output tail), finish the remaining steps and write outputs/response.md reporting the unverified part. NEVER let a hung child hold the deliverable hostage: validation CI on the pull request is the safety net"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 --> B7 end USE --> SHELLSTATE SHELLSTATE --> CWD CWD --> BGJOBS ``` ## github_comment_format.md # GitHub tracker comment Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must render natively on GitHub. - Headings: `##`, `###` - Bullets: `- item` - Numbered lists: `1. item` - Bold: `**text**` - Inline code: `` `code` `` - Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`bash`, `json`, `text`) - Link: `[text](url)` - Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row) Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no `{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable. **IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER` (the composite key form works directly).

You are Fa, a coding agent (also called fa). Never refer to yourself as pi, Claude, or any other assistant name. You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness. Use the read, write, ls, and bash tools to inspect and modify files and run commands. Be concise.

## Session recall — never answer about the past from assumption

1. **Reference = search.** When the user references any past decision, rule, task, or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made", "that issue from last week"), call `session_search` BEFORE answering. Never answer about the past from assumption.
2. **Resume ritual.** After a compaction boundary is crossed or the session resumes, read the obligations ledger block (the `<system-notice>` titled "obligations ledger") first; it is the contract of what is still owed.
3. **Commit in the open.** Before promising a follow-up, check the ledger. When you arm a timer or watch (`schedule_message`), state the reason clearly in the message text — the engine writes a `pending-wait` ledger entry from it, and the fired timer re-enters a context that knows why it exists.
4. **Durable ≠ session.** Cross-session rules go to long-term memory immediately (`memory_add`); session-scoped obligations stay in the ledger. Never misuse either layer for the other.
5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## Working set — your status, pinned

The `<working-set source="agent">` block at the end of this prompt is YOUR working set: the short status you keep with the `working_set` tool. It is re-sent with every request and survives compaction, resume and a restart — when older records are folded away, your status is not.

**Keep in it:** decisions made and why; the red list (what must never be done — owner gates, scopes, files not to touch); failing tests and their cause; the next steps in order; rules you must keep (commit identity, hook rules, branch, worktree).

**Update it when something changes** — a decision, a new red test, a changed next step — at the `context ≈85%` notice, and before a `reply` that ends your turn. Replace the whole text each time (the newest call wins); `working_set("")` clears it. The cap is 4096 chars: a longer text is refused, not clipped — shorten it and call again.

**It is notes, not instructions.** Nothing in it grants an approval, unlocks a tool or changes a rule: only real user input authorizes, and every side effect still passes the approval that applies to the real tool. Never put secrets in it (the session redactor masks what it recognises; the result reports `redacted: N`).

**It is not memory.** The working set is what the next request of THIS session must know; a fact a future session needs goes to long-term memory (`memory_add`).

**Context notices come from the harness, with its own numbers:**

- `compacted: N records hidden; context now ≈X/W …` — older records were folded; the full history stays in the session file (`session_search`, `compact_expand`). Your working set is pinned above: continue the task instead of re-reading what was folded. With no working set yet, write one now, then continue.
- `context ≈85% (≈X/W): update your working set … KEEP WORKING` — the context is filling; the fold is still ahead. Update the working set with decisions, red tests and next steps and keep working: compaction will fold older records, and the pinned working set carries you across it.

## Context hygiene — keep the window for the task

Tool results fill the context far faster than your own text. Each rule below is tied to what it costs when ignored.

1. **Read ≤ 50 lines at a time.** Use `read` with `offset`/`limit` or a `:A-B` selector; slice shell output with `cut -c1-120`. An 80–100-line slice costs 5–10 KB per call.
2. **Locate first, then read a window.** `grep -n` for the symbol, then read about 20 lines around the hit. Never read a whole file to find one line.
3. **Pipe test output through `grep`/`tail`.** A full test log is thousands of lines; the failures and the summary line are under 2 KB.
4. **Check jobs by id.** `bash_job` with the job `id` — never the full status listing (about 9.5 KB per call, and it lists other workers' jobs).
5. **Think short.** Do not restate tool output in your thinking; decide in about 150 words per step, then act. Long thinking blocks cost 350–3,500 reasoning tokens per turn and stay in the context.
6. **Keep your working set current.** Update it when a decision, a red test or the next step changes — the `context ≈85%` notice is the last call, not the first.

## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
2.6. **Conformance coverage** — applies ONLY when the final claim includes behavioral conformance: "matches the reference/specification", parity with an existing implementation, protocol/format compliance — any domain. Happy-path agreement certifies nothing about rejection paths or option combinations: two implementations agreeing on every well-formed input can still diverge exactly where one of them must say no. A conformance item counts as verified only when the checklist also quotes **negative and combination checks**, each one actually run and quoted in its ledger row: inputs that must be rejected or must error, combinations of incompatible/mutually exclusive options that must be refused, empty and corrupt inputs, boundary values, "must NOT work" / "must not find" cases — alongside the happy paths. A blanket "everything matches" without such coverage is not verified: mark the item `fail` and run the missing cases.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the working directory; returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total) as [bash attempt N]; environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output. For long-running commands (builds, servers, watchers) pass background: true — you get the job id immediately and a notice when it finishes; check progress with bash_job. A foreground command still running when the user sends a message is moved to a background job untouched (never killed). A command still running after 60s is moved to a background job automatically (never restarted); carried timeouts are NOT auto-retried — retry if the completion notice reports a timeout. A `cmd &`/nohup survivor of a call is adopted as a tracked job (completion reported; no captured output or exit code).

tools.name: bash_job
tools.description: Manage background shell jobs (from bash background: true, and adopted cmd & / nohup survivors). Actions: "status" lists running + last 20 exited (all: true = every job; id = one), "output" tails a log (id, lines), "stop" kills a running job (id).

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return ranked results with [n] citation markers, titles, URLs, and snippets. Runs a provider chain (DuckDuckGo first, keyed providers when configured) and falls through on failure. Follow up with web_fetch on a result URL to read the full page.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its main content as Markdown: headings, link anchors, lists, and code blocks are preserved, navigation and boilerplate are stripped. Known sites (pub.dev) are rendered via dedicated handlers. Use it to read pages found with web_search.

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search long-term memory for relevant facts, preferences, or past decisions. Use proactively before tasks that might benefit from prior context.

tools.name: working_set
tools.description: Save your working set: the short status (decisions made, never-do list, next steps, rules to keep) pinned into the system prompt of every request. It survives compaction and resume; the newest replaces the previous one; "" clears it. Max 4096 chars — longer text is refused, not clipped.

tools.name: reply
tools.description:
Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

tools.name: session_search
tools.description: Search the WHOLE session archive (every past turn — hidden, compacted and checkpointed regions included), not just the current context. Use it whenever the user references a past decision, rule, task or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made") BEFORE answering from assumption. Returns pointers (id, kind, timestamp, preview), never full content — pull the record back with compact_expand. With mode: "map" it reports the archive structure instead: record-kind counts, hidden/checkpoint totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth.

tools.name: others
tools.description: Deferred tools (not loaded): agent_directory, agent_message, ask, checkpoint, compact_expand, config, memory_delete, memory_list, request_secret, rewind, schedule_message, task, task_cancel, task_observe, task_resume, task_send, task_status. Call others with tool_name to load a tool's full description and schema; omit tool_name to list them with one-line docs.

## Description

**Failed/cancelled jobs:** Build native binaries (self-hosted, macos-m5, macos, arm64, tar) [cancelled], Sign release checksums [failure], Advance vpinned marker [failure]
**Run:** https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/46024478783

Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/46035867876) · started 16:44 · done 17:38 ✅

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 2456
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2456
- **Title**: gh-2455 [ci-red] v1.0.788 failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2455` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +52
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-11-27T17:38:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-11-27T17:59:08Z

## PR Description

Closes #2455
### Root Cause
- The v1.0.788 tag run (46024478783) hung the arm64 macOS `binaries` leg for 44 min inside the checkout `git fetch` on the self-hosted `fa-m5-2` runner; the job's `timeout-minutes: 45` kill landed at 16:41:02Z, so `fa-macos-arm64.tar.gz` was never produced (degraded-runner class, gh-2314 precedent).
- `Sign release checksums` and `Advance vpinned marker` then failed **as designed** (gh-1832 asset gate; `pin_release` provenance gate) — a partial release must never publish.
- Systemic gap: the degraded-runner watchdog settled at 15:45:21Z — *before* the binaries leg even started (15:56:02Z) — because `binaries`/`web-spa`/`build-extension` (the three gh-1832 asset producers) were not in its `needs`. Its scan saw the leg still `conclusion: null` (in-flight jobs are filtered from the kill signature), tripped nothing, and the gh-2290 tag-arm retrigger never fired: the train sat red with no self-heal.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_check.sh — the gh-2290 timeout-kill trip decision for the
# `watchdog` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml (issue #194 point 4).
#
# The watchdog's remedy for a degraded-runner allocation is ONE retrigger
# with a fresh allocation (never `gh run rerun`). Tripping requires
# recognizing a job-level timeout KILL — and only that kill. The v1.0.745
# tag run 4424840840 hung a PTY shard (the pty2 blocking-waitpid wedge,
# `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`), burned
# its 40-minute budget and was killed by `timeout-minutes`: GitHub landed
# that kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (NOT `failure` — jobs
# 134588877581/134566192421) with the mid-flight step `cancelled` and the
# trailing `if: always()` evidence steps `skipped`.
#
# gh-2358 added the SECOND kill shape: runner DEATH. The v1.0.759 tag run
# (44868070949, job 136736814346) lost its self-hosted runner `fa-m5-1`
# ~11 minutes into `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)` ("The
# self-hosted runner lost communication with the server"). GitHub
# concluded the JOB `failure` but NOTHING ever reported again: the
# mid-flight step — and every trailing step — froze at conclusion `null`,
# so the `cancelled`-step-only signature was blind to it. The watchdog
# ran, found nothing, and the release train sat red (no GitHub release,
# `vpinned` marker stuck) until a manual full rerun. One trip decision,
# two kill shapes: the mid-flight cut is `cancelled` (GitHub concluded
# the cancel) or `null` (nothing ever concluded).
#
# The degraded-runner-kill signature, as one predicate over the jobs JSON:
#
#   job conclusion == "failure" OR "cancelled"      (both kill shapes land)
#   AND at least one step concluded "cancelled" OR "null"
#     (a step was cut mid-flight — the kill itself; `null` is the
#     frozen runner-death tail, gh-2358)
#   AND NO step concluded "failure"                  (a real test failure
#     ENDS with a failed step — in these shards the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps often trail it with `success` — so a genuine red
#     never trips; a fresh runner allocation cannot fix a defect. This
#     guard also covers death AFTER a real red: the failed step is
#     concluded, only the trailing steps freeze at `null`)
#
# A cancelled job with NO steps (never started — a run-level cancel
# reaching a queued job) is NOT a kill (`any()` over an empty steps
# array is false). Success/skipped never trip. A job whose conclusion
# is still null is in flight — the first select filters it out, so an
# in-progress leg can never fake the signature.
#
# Network-free by contract: the caller fetches the run's jobs document in
# ONE call (the jobs API embeds each job's steps array — `gh run view
# --json jobs`; `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` is fine unpaged, but
# `--paginate` concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first
# page — verified against a 69-job run) and hands the FILE here.
# Fixture-self-tested by scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh (#1100
# pattern), wired into the static gate; the workflow wiring is pinned by
# test/ci_watchdog_tag_retrigger_guard_test.dart.
#
# Usage: watchdog_trip_check.sh [jobs-json-file] [output-file]
#   jobs-json-file  the jobs document; `-` or an empty arg reads stdin
#   output-file     default $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set (the trip=<bool> line
#                   lands there AND on stdout); without one, stdout only.
#                   Diagnostics never start with `trip=`, so the line is
#                   unambiguous in both sinks.
set -u

json_file="${1:--}"
out_file="${2:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}}"

if [ "$json_file" = "-" ] || [ -z "$json_file" ]; then
  jobs_json="$(cat)"
else
  jobs_json="$(cat "$json_file")"
fi

# The degraded-runner-kill signature, as ONE shared jq filter (the count
# and the diagnostics below project over the same filter — a duplicated
# literal can drift silently, and the selftest pins only the trip=
# contract): failed-or-cancelled jobs with a mid-flight cut (>=1 step
# concluded `cancelled` OR frozen unconcluded `null`) and NO failed step.
filter='.jobs[]?
   | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
   | select(any(.steps[]?; .conclusion == "cancelled" or .conclusion == null))
   | select(all(.steps[]?; .conclusion != "failure"))'

matches="$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "[$filter] | length")"

if [ -z "$matches" ] || ! [ "$matches" -eq "$matches" ] 2>/dev/null; then
  # A malformed projection must NEVER flip the trip (fail-safe: the
  # watchdog is an optimization — a broken pre-check degrades to no
  # retrigger, never to a spurious dispatch loop).
  echo "::warning::watchdog_trip_check: unparseable jobs JSON or jq failure — not tripping"
  matches=0
fi

trip=false
if [ "$matches" -gt 0 ]; then
  trip=true
fi

if [ "$trip" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::notice::watchdog_trip_check: $matches job(s) match the degraded-runner-kill signature (gh-2290/gh-2358):"
  printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r "[$filter]
    | (.[] | \"  \" + .name + \": \" + .conclusion
       + \" (mid-flight cut: \"
       + ([.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == \"cancelled\" or .conclusion == null) | .name] | join(\", \"))
       + \")\")
  "
else
  echo "watchdog_trip_check: no degraded-runner-kill signature — nothing to retrigger"
fi

if [ -n "$out_file" ]; then
  {
    printf 'trip=%s\n' "$trip"
  } >> "$out_file"
fi
echo "trip=$trip"

# gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
====
  # never attach to the actual release commit.
  web-spa:
    name: Build web SPA bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive asset: a web-build failure (guard trip, SDK flake) must NOT
    # hold the release hostage — CLI provenance (SHA256SUMS) and the vpinned
    # bump still ship. Job-level continue-on-error reports the job (and its
    # check) as SUCCESS — the failed steps stay visible on the run page for
    # the manual check. Downstream needs see success; the provenance fa-*
    # sweep then deterministically finds no zip (success -> signed,
    # failure -> absent — never a half-updated manifest).
    continue-on-error: true
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach fa-web-spa.zip to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
====
  # no matter when the daily leg ran; the daily leg keeps pre-staging the
  # next-tag draft and stays the n_1012 emergency producer.
  build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension (release)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Additive REQUIRED asset, same semantics as web-spa: an SDK flake or
    # vendor-fetch hiccup must NOT hold CLI provenance hostage — the
    # release-provenance required-assets gate (gh-1832) is the single
    # publish blocker and strands the draft loudly on the MISSING asset
    # (previous release stays latest). continue-on-error keeps the check
    # green; the failed steps stay visible on the run page.
    continue-on-error: true
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach fa-extension.zip to the GitHub Release
    steps:

watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. app-crap-gate rides
    # along too (gh-2389, v1.0.768 run 45302423375): its 6-minute timeout
    # kill landed 18 s AFTER the scan completed (the leg was not in `needs`,
    # so the watchdog settled as soon as coverage-gate did) — trip=false,
    # no one-shot retrigger, no self-heal. They must all be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    # gh-2455: the release-asset producer legs ride along too — binaries,
    # web-spa, build-extension, the three producers of the gh-1832
    # required-asset set (fa-macos-*/fa-linux-*/fa-windows-*,
    # fa-web-spa.zip, fa-extension.zip). The v1.0.788 tag run
    # (46024478783) hung the arm64 macOS binaries leg in its checkout
    # `git fetch` for 44 min and the `timeout-minutes: 45` kill landed at
    # 16:41:02Z — 56 minutes AFTER the watchdog had settled (15:45:21Z;
    # binaries only STARTS once quality-gate does, ~15:51-15:56): the scan
    # ran against a document where the leg was still `conclusion: null`
    # (in-flight jobs are filtered out of the kill signature), trip=false,
    # no dispatch, and the release train sat red on the missing
    # fa-macos-arm64.tar.gz (gh-1832 refused to sign, pin_release refused
    # to move vpinned) until a manual rerun. With the producers in
    # `needs`, the same kill shape (cancelled job + cancelled checkout
    # step + no failed step — verified against the real run's jobs JSON)
    # trips the scan and the gh-2290 tag-arm dispatch rebuilds the
    # missing asset on a fresh allocation. Skipped producers (PR arm,
    # deduped twins) satisfy `needs` as `skipped` — no added latency
    # there.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, app-crap-gate, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual, binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
    # release gate (gh-2290).
    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    permissions:
      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
      contents: write
    steps:
      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# watchdog_trip_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-2290 watchdog
# trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh, the `watchdog` job in
# ci.yml).
#
# The v1.0.745 tag run (4424840840) hung a PTY shard on the pty2
# blocking-waitpid wedge (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode
# to check in`), burned its whole 40-minute budget, was concluded
# `cancelled` — and NOTHING retrigged: the watchdog was pull_request-only
# AND its detector scanned failure-conclusion jobs only. The decision must
# trip exactly on the timeout-kill signature and never on a genuine red.
# Proves, on fixture JSON (no network, no gh, no token):
#   AC1  the gh-2290 kill mode: job conclusion `cancelled`, the
#     mid-flight step `cancelled`, trailing `if: always()` evidence
#     steps `skipped` — the EXACT shape of hung shard jobs
#     134588877581/134566192421 → trip,
#   AC2  the classic kill mode: job `failure`, a cut `cancelled` step,
#     no failed step → trip,
#   AC3  the gh-2358 runner-death kill mode: the box (fa-m5-1, v1.0.759
#     tag run 44868070949, job 136736814346) lost communication ~11 min
#     into `flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)`; the JOB concluded
#     `failure` and the mid-flight step — with every trailing step —
#     froze at conclusion `null` (never reported). One trip decision,
#     two kill shapes: the mid-flight cut is `cancelled` (GitHub
#     concluded the cancel) or `null` (nothing ever concluded).
#   FC1  a REAL test failure never trips — in either landing shape: the
#     failed step LAST, or the failed step TRAILED by the `if: always()`
#     evidence steps (`success`) that every red pty shard actually
#     leaves behind (last-step-success — the old last-step detector was
#     blind to this too),
#   FC2  success / skipped / a cancelled never-started job (no steps) /
#     an empty jobs array never trip,
#   FC3  a malformed body fails SAFE to trip=false with a warning (a
#     broken pre-check must degrade to no retrigger, never to a
#     spurious dispatch loop),
#   FC4  the runner died AFTER a real test failure — the red step
#     concluded `failure` and only the trailing steps froze at `null`:
#     a genuine red must never trip, regardless of the frozen tail.
#   RG   the output contract: exactly ONE `trip=<bool>` line, no
#     diagnostic masquerading as `trip=`, GITHUB_OUTPUT lands exactly
#     one line, multiple matches still produce a single line, and the
#     stdin arm (`-`) works.
# Same discipline as release_dedupe_selftest.sh (gh-1625, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/watchdog_trip_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

fixture() { # fixture <name> <json> — write a fixture, run the check
  _fx_name="$1"; shift
  printf '%s' "$1" > "$TMP/$_fx_name.json"
  bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/$_fx_name.json" 2>&1
}

trip_line() { # trip_line <output> — the trip= line, empty when absent
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -E '^trip=(true|false)$' | head -1
}

trip_count() { # trip_count <output> — number of trip= lines
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$'
}

json_for() { # json_for <conclusion> <shape: kill|failure|success>
  # kill:    the REAL gh-2290 shape — the mid-flight dart test step
  #          cancelled, the trailing if:always() evidence steps skipped.
  # death:   the REAL gh-2358 runner-death shape — the mid-flight
  #          flutter build ios step and everything after it froze at
  #          conclusion null (the runner never reported anything again).
  # failure: a real test failure — the dart test step FAILED, the
  #          evidence steps still trail with success (the last step is
  #          NOT the failed one in these shards).
  # success: a clean job.
  case "$2" in
    kill)    steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "upload artifact", "conclusion": "skipped"}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": "skipped"}]' ;;
    death)   steps='[{"name": "flutter build ios (debug, unsigned)", "conclusion": null}, {"name": "Post Run ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get", "conclusion": null}, {"name": "Post Cache CocoaPods (iOS)", "conclusion": null}]' ;;
    failure) steps='[{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
    *)       steps='[{"name": "run", "conclusion": "success"}]' ;;
  esac
  cat <<JEOF
{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)", "conclusion": "$1", "steps": $steps}]}
JEOF
}

echo "watchdog_trip_selftest (gh-2290):"

# AC1 — the gh-2290 kill mode (the REAL shape: conclusion cancelled,
# mid-flight step cancelled, trailing always()-evidence steps skipped).
out="$(fixture ac1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC1 cancelled job with a cancelled step trips (gh-2290 kill mode)" $?

# AC2 — the classic kill mode (failure conclusion, cut step, no failed step).
out="$(fixture ac2 "$(json_for failure kill)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC2 failure job with a cancelled step and no failed step trips" $?

# AC3 — the gh-2358 runner-death kill mode (the REAL shape: fa-m5-1
# lost communication ~11 min into the flutter build ios step of tag
# run 44868070949, job 136736814346; the JOB concluded failure and the
# mid-flight step — with every trailing step — froze at null).
out="$(fixture ac3 "$(json_for failure death)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC3 failure job with an UNCONCLUDED (null) mid-flight step trips (gh-2358 runner death)" $?

# AC3b — the same runner death under the cancelled conclusion (a
# run-level cancel racing the lost heartbeat): still a mid-flight cut,
# still no failed step.
out="$(fixture ac3b "$(json_for cancelled death)")"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "AC3b cancelled job with an unconcluded (null) mid-flight step trips" $?

# FC1 — a real test failure must NOT retrigger (both landing shapes).
out="$(fixture fc1a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 0/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1a real test failure (failed step, trailing evidence) does NOT trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc1b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 3/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "setup", "conclusion": "success"}, {"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC1b real test failure (failed LAST step) does NOT trip" $?

# FC4 — the runner died AFTER a real test failure: the red step
# concluded `failure`, then the box vanished before the trailing
# always() evidence steps reported — they froze at null. A genuine red
# must never trip regardless of the frozen tail (a fresh runner
# allocation cannot fix a defect).
out="$(fixture fc4 '{"jobs": [{"name": "Core tests (shard 1/4)", "conclusion": "failure", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "failure"}, {"name": "junit durations", "conclusion": null}, {"name": "Post cache", "conclusion": null}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC4 failed step + frozen trailing steps (death after a real red) does NOT trip" $?

# FC2 — clean, skipped, never-started, empty.
out="$(fixture fc2a '{"jobs": [{"name": "Static gates", "conclusion": "success", "steps": [{"name": "analyze", "conclusion": "success"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2a success job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2b '{"jobs": [{"name": "Golden suite (macOS baselines)", "conclusion": "skipped", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2b skipped job does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2c '{"jobs": [{"name": "Binaries smoke gate", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": []}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2c cancelled never-started job (no steps) does not trip" $?

out="$(fixture fc2d '{"jobs": []}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC2d empty jobs array does not trip" $?

# FC3 — malformed body fails safe.
out="$(fixture fc3 'not json at all')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=false" ]
check "FC3 malformed jobs JSON fails safe to trip=false" $?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '::warning::'
check "FC3 malformed body warns loudly" $?

# RG — output contract.
out="$(fixture rg1 "$(json_for cancelled kill)")"
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG1 exactly one trip= line on stdout" $?

printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -vE '^trip=' | grep -qE '^trip='
[ $? -ne 0 ]
check "RG2 no diagnostic line masquerades as trip=" $?

out_file="$TMP/github_output"
: > "$out_file"
GITHUB_OUTPUT="$out_file" bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/ac1.json" > "$TMP/rg3.out"
grep -cE '^trip=(true|false)$' "$out_file" > "$TMP/rg3.count"
[ "$(cat "$TMP/rg3.count")" = "1" ]
check "RG3 exactly one trip= line lands in GITHUB_OUTPUT" $?

out="$(fixture rg4 '{"jobs": [{"name": "PTY shard 2/3", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "upload", "conclusion": "skipped"}]}, {"name": "PTY shard 0/3", "conclusion": "cancelled", "steps": [{"name": "dart test", "conclusion": "cancelled"}, {"name": "upload", "conclusion": "skipped"}]}]}')"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
[ "$(trip_count "$out")" = "1" ]
check "RG4 multiple matches trip once, one line" $?

# RG5 — stdin arm (`-`).
out="$(printf '%s' "$(json_for cancelled kill)" | bash "$CHECK" - 2>&1)"
[ "$(trip_line "$out")" = "trip=true" ]
check "RG5 stdin arm trips" $?

if [ "$fails" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: $fails FAILURE(S)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "watchdog_trip_selftest: all green"

# required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
====
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

   - `135885361973` "Build web SPA bundle" → `conclusion: "failure"` (step "Upload bundle to GitHub Release" = `failure`, trailing steps `success`)
   Both jobs carried job-level `continue-on-error: true` at that commit (`ci.yml:4731`/`:4857` of `5f6902ce939`). The masking reaches the check-run rollup, **not** the `conclusion` field of the `/actions/runs/<id>/jobs` document the watchdog scans.
2. **Runner source** — `ApplyContinueOnError` (actions/runner `src/Runner.Worker/ExecutionContext.cs:1424`) bails out unless `Result == TaskResult.Failed`: it masks **only** Failed→Succeeded and leaves `Canceled` untouched. A `timeout-minutes` kill is a cancellation, not a step failure — the v1.0.745 precedent (run 4424840840) already landed such a kill as job conclusion `cancelled` (the gh-2290 shape).
3. Therefore a `timeout-minutes` kill on `web-spa`/`build-extension` lands **`cancelled` + cancelled mid-flight step + no failed step** — exactly the signature `watchdog_trip_check.sh` already trips on. A masked-to-success landing does not exist in the jobs document (counterproof: CK2's raw `failure` above).

Fix `a6001699d3` adds the fixtures — deliberately **without** widening the filter:

`watchdog_trip_check.sh` is fail-safe by doctrine ("a broken pre-check must degrade to no retrigger, never to a spurious dispatch loop"). The finding asked for one confirmation + a fixture.
